findings.title: camelCase function name
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires all functions to use snake_case. `applyFilterExpression` uses camelCase.
findings.fix: Rename to `apply_filter_expression` and update the import and call site in app.py.

findings.title: Import of camelCase function name
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires snake_case for functions. Importing `applyFilterExpression` propagates a naming violation into app.py.
findings.evidence: from utils import slugify, truncate, parse_tags, applyFilterExpression
findings.fix: Once utils.py is corrected (STY-1), update this import to `apply_filter_expression`.

findings.title: camelCase function name
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires snake_case for functions. `isAdmin` uses camelCase.
findings.fix: Rename to `is_admin` and update the import and call site in app.py.

findings.title: Predicate named with camelCase violating rule 1.4
findings.why: Rule 1.4 states boolean-returning functions must read as predicates using snake_case: `is_admin`, `has_access`. `isAdmin` is camelCase and does not follow the prescribed snake_case predicate form.

findings.title: Import of camelCase predicate function name
findings.why: Rule 1.1 and 1.4 both require the function to be named `is_admin`. Importing `isAdmin` imports the violation.
findings.evidence: from auth import current_user_id, isAdmin, hash_password, verify_password
findings.fix: Once auth.py is corrected (STY-3/STY-4), update this import to `is_admin`.

findings.title: Bare `except:` clause
findings.why: Rule 4.1 forbids bare `except:`. It catches every possible exception including `SystemExit`, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `GeneratorExit`, masking serious failures.
findings.fix: Replace with the narrowest applicable exception type, e.g. `except sqlite3.DatabaseError as e:`, then log or surface the error.

findings.title: `except` block contains only `pass`
findings.why: Rule 4.2 forbids an except block that contains only `pass`. If the error is genuinely ignorable, the rule requires logging it and a comment explaining why.
findings.fix: At minimum log the exception (e.g. `logging.warning("delete_note failed: %s", e)`) and add a comment justifying why the error is safe to suppress.

findings.title: Traceback returned in HTTP response body
findings.why: Rule 4.3 explicitly forbids returning an exception's message or traceback in an HTTP response. `traceback.format_exc()` exposes internal stack frames to callers.
findings.fix: Remove the `"trace"` key entirely. Return only a generic error message to the caller; log the traceback server-side.

findings.title: Standard-library import not separated from third-party imports by a blank line
findings.why: Rule 2.2 requires import order: stdlib → (blank line) → third-party → (blank line) → first-party. `import traceback` (stdlib) appears on line 2 immediately before the blank line and first-party imports, but `from flask import ...` (third-party) is on line 1 with no blank line separating stdlib from third-party. The stdlib block (`from flask` is third-party; `import traceback` is stdlib) is out of order: traceback should precede flask with a blank line between them.
findings.evidence:
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import traceback

from config import DEBUG, PAGE_SIZE, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH
findings.fix:
Reorder so stdlib comes first, then a blank line, then third-party (flask), then a blank line, then first-party imports:

import traceback

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

from config import ...
from db import ...
from auth import ...
from utils import ...

findings.title: Wildcard import (pre-existing)
findings.why: Rule 2.1 forbids wildcard imports. `from config import *` makes every name in config.py available without any indication of origin, defeating static analysis.
findings.fix: Replace with explicit imports of only the names db.py actually uses, e.g. `from config import DATABASE_URL`.

findings.title: camelCase function name (pre-existing)
findings.why: Rule 1.1 requires snake_case for functions. `insertNote` uses camelCase. This is pre-existing but still a live violation in the post-patch file.
findings.fix: Rename to `insert_note` and update all call sites (app.py line 34).

findings.title: Mutable default argument `tags=[]` (pre-existing)
findings.why: Rule 3.1 forbids mutable default arguments. The list `[]` is created once at definition time and shared across every call that omits `tags`.
findings.fix: Change the signature to `def insertNote(title, body, user_id, tags=None):` and add `if tags is None: tags = []` at the top of the body.
